server.name: nyc-council-mcp
server.title: NYC Council legislation MCP server
server.description: An MCP server for New York City Council legislation, votes, hearings, committees and members. Live tools ask the Council's Legistar API when you ask; local tools answer from an index built from a public archive of Legistar; member facts no official source publishes in one place are curated by BetaNYC and labeled as not official. Nothing is invented: a value with no source is left blank.

sources.title: Legistar, live
sources.what: Bills, their history and files, hearings and agendas, committees, roll-call votes and member contact details, fetched from the Council's API when asked.
sources.how_gathered: Read-only requests to the Council's own API at the moment you ask. Needs LEGISTAR_TOKEN; a server without one has no live tools.

terms.credit_line: Source: New York City Council, Legistar.

caveats: Legistar sometimes changes a meeting's status without updating its timestamp; upcoming_events checks status live when it can.
A known-bad Legistar profile link (PersonWWW2) is corrected from a small dated list in the code, with the original kept in PersonWWW2_upstream. Other values are passed on as the API returns them.
get_council_member adds BetaNYC's curated facts (topics party, wikidata, social) and, with a local index, districts (topic districts). Those are separate sources.

sources.title: Bills and their history
sources.what: Introductions, resolutions and land use items: titles, summaries, full text, sponsors, Local Law numbers, attachments and history.
sources.how_gathered: This server answers from a local SQLite index, with no network call. The index is built from a clone of jehiah/nyc_legislation (https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_legislation), an unofficial mirror that copies the Council's Legistar records through the Legistar API. Every local answer ends with a line naming when the index was built and the archive commit it was built from.

changes.detail: Records are restructured into database tables with their values unchanged. aggregate_bills counts bills by a field, and co_sponsors counts the bills each pair of members sponsored together.

terms.license_name: None stated by the publisher; the jehiah/nyc_legislation archive states no license either
terms.credit_line: Source: New York City Council, Legistar.

caveats: The jehiah/nyc_legislation archive is not the Council's: it is an independent copy, and it can lag Legistar. How current shows when this server's index was built; the archive commit it was built from, which is how current the copy is, is named at the end of every local answer.
An empty local answer means 'not in this index', not 'does not exist'.

sources.title: Council terms and districts
sources.what: Every Council term since 1999, with its district.
sources.source_name: City Council Members (1999 to Present), NYC Open Data dataset uvw5-9znb
sources.how_gathered: The Council publishes this dataset on NYC Open Data, the City's open data portal. A copy ships with this server (data/council-member-terms.json) and is loaded into the local index. A monthly job re-fetches it and opens a pull request when the rows change.

changes.detail: The rows are used as published, loaded into the index and joined to Legistar people on person ID, never on names. district_member works out who held a district on a date from them.

coverage.geography: New York City Council districts 1 to 51, every term since 1999
known_gaps: The City updates this file late. A seat that looks vacant may have a new member; the answer then names anyone Legistar lists who is missing from the file.

terms.license_name: No restrictions on use: NYC Administrative Code § 23-502(d) (the Open Data Law, Local Law 11 of 2012)
terms.credit_line: Source: New York City Council, City Council Members (1999 to Present), NYC Open Data uvw5-9znb, in the snapshot dated by about_data; used as published.

caveats: How current is when this server's copy was fetched from NYC Open Data.
District lines are redrawn, so a past district number may not match today's map.

sources.title: Party: every ballot line won on
sources.what: Every ballot line each sitting member won on, with its votes (NYC has fusion voting).
sources.source_name: NYC Board of Elections certified results
sources.how_gathered: Curated by BetaNYC: lines and votes copied from the Board's certified 'Statement and Return Report for Certification' for the election that gave each member their seat, with a link to that document on each row. Never inferred from a caucus or from Wikidata. Shipped in data/council-party.json; nothing is looked up at run time.

changes.detail: Hand-collected per member from certified results, then re-checked: all 50 general-election rows were compared by script with the Board's CSVs (no differences). Each row records its source, check date, status and second check.

coverage.geography: The 51 members seated on the check date

terms.credit_line: Party lines from NYC Board of Elections certified results, curated by BetaNYC.

caveats: Most errors here would be in BetaNYC's copying or matching, so report them first at https://github.com/BetaNYC/nyc-council-mcp/issues. To check a row, use its Board of Elections certified results document (each row links it).
How current is the date BetaNYC last checked the file, not a build date.
Each row says how sure it is: status verified (50 rows) or likely (1 row), and how it was checked a second time (second_check). No person has reviewed the rows one by one.
A Council special election is nonpartisan: its lines are names the candidates chose, and the row says so.

sources.title: Wikidata and Wikipedia
sources.what: The Wikidata item and English Wikipedia article for each sitting member.
sources.how_gathered: Curated by BetaNYC: each item was checked to be a person whose English Wikipedia article names their Council district. Shipped in data/council-wikidata.json; nothing is looked up at run time.

changes.detail: Hand-matched per member, then every row re-checked against Wikidata and Wikipedia. Party is not taken from Wikidata.

coverage.geography: The 51 members seated on the check date

terms.license_name: CC0 1.0 (Wikidata structured data). Only links to Wikipedia articles are used, no article text (that text is CC BY-SA).

caveats: Most errors here would be in BetaNYC's copying or matching, so report them first at https://github.com/BetaNYC/nyc-council-mcp/issues. To check a row, use the Wikidata item and Wikipedia article each row links.
How current is the date BetaNYC last checked the file, not a build date.
All 51 rows have status verified, and each records its second check (second_check). No person has reviewed the rows one by one.

sources.title: Office social accounts
sources.what: Council office accounts on Bluesky, Instagram, Threads and LinkedIn.
sources.source_name: council.nyc.gov member pages and the Council's Bluesky starter pack; the account's own profile last
sources.how_gathered: Curated by BetaNYC: office accounts only, never campaign or personal. 'verified' means council.nyc.gov links it, or it is in the Council's Bluesky starter pack and is not a personal or campaign account; 'likely' means only the account's own bio says it is the office, and nothing official confirms it. Shipped in data/council-social.json; nothing is looked up at run time.

changes.detail: Hand-collected per member. Every 'likely' account was re-checked independently for an official source naming the handle, and each likely account records the result in second_check.

coverage.geography: The 51 members seated on the check date
known_gaps: Facebook and X are out of scope.
Several Threads profiles could not be read without logging in; each row's notes say which.

caveats: Most errors here would be in BetaNYC's copying or matching, so report them first at https://github.com/BetaNYC/nyc-council-mcp/issues. To check a row, use council.nyc.gov or the account itself (each account links its source).
How current is the date BetaNYC last checked the file, not a build date.
Of 69 accounts, 49 have status verified and 20 likely. The 20 likely accounts rest only on the account's own bio. No person has reviewed the rows one by one.
